title: VLANs: why the camera can't see the NAS
summary: Two networks on one switch, what keeps them apart, and what joins them.

sources.claim: A VLAN splits one physical LAN into separate broadcast domains, and devices in different VLANs need a router to reach each other.
sources.cite: Juniper Networks, Understanding Bridging and VLANs on Switches (page dated 24 March 2025)

sources.claim: On Junos the last security policy is the default policy, which denies all traffic.
sources.cite: Juniper Networks, Reordering Security Policies (page dated 13 November 2024)

steps.title: Two networks on one switch
steps.body: In this office the cameras plug into the same switch as the desks and the NAS, switch-1, but they sit in their own VLAN, 30. The desks, the printer, the NAS and the Wi-Fi are in VLAN 10. A VLAN is a separate network inside a switch: its devices only hear each other.

steps.title: Same VLAN
steps.after: Both cameras are in VLAN 30, so switch-1 joins them directly. No router or firewall is involved.

steps.title: Different VLANs
steps.prompt: Now trace from camera-1 to nas-1.
steps.after: This time the path leaves VLAN 30, goes up to fw-1 and comes back down into VLAN 10: devices in different VLANs only meet at a router or firewall. On the fw-1 hop Fathom says no policy from cameras to trust is in the design, so it cannot say what fw-1 does with this traffic. On Junos the last, default policy denies all traffic, which is why the camera can't see the NAS.

steps.title: What joins them
steps.prompt: Click the device that joins VLAN 10 and VLAN 30.
steps.hint: Look for the device with a cable into each VLAN and an address in each network.
steps.after: fw-1 has an interface in each network, 192.168.10.1 and 192.168.30.1. Traffic between the two VLANs can only cross there, where its policies are read.

steps.title: Break it on purpose
steps.prompt: Make a mistake on purpose. Open Inventory, then Networks, open VLAN 10 and detach switch-2 port 1. Then Add network: a VLAN with id 30, on switch-2, port 1. Save, and watch this step.
steps.after: Checks warns: the desk run now has VLAN 10 at switch-1 and VLAN 30 at switch-2. A cable between two access ports joins their VLANs, so the desks and the cameras would share one network.

steps.title: Put it back
steps.prompt: Put it back: in VLAN 30 detach switch-2 port 1, then add it to VLAN 10 the same way.
steps.after: Clear again. A VLAN keeps devices apart on one switch, and only a router or firewall joins two VLANs.
